card.name: Commas after counts in old science
card.fires_on: A comma that follows a clause giving a number, a measurement, or a count of parts, in old-style textbook prose on anatomy, chemistry or geography. It is usually followed by a list or a relative clause.

modes.label: Comma after a count of parts
modes.description: Comma after a phrase naming how many zones, states or surfaces there are, before the items are listed.

modes.description: Comma after a compound or atom statement in early chemistry text, before the makeup is given.
